gen-gf-revalia-gf-courier-prime: Courier Prime keeps a drafting-pen line going, with lowercase that fills most of its height and generous round letters. Courier Prime is a monospace body that skims along smoothly, while Revalia up top sprawls wide and loud.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-days-one: Chunky and loose, Revalia strides across the line with an open-tailed g, and Days One sits under it with a sturdy, rope-ladder rhythm. And its tall x-height gives the pair a hefty, friendly punch.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-epunda-sans: Bold, with a relaxed stride between its widely separated letters, Revalia leads while Epunda Sans follows in oversized, daylight-filled curves. Revalia earns its place big and brief.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-farro: Loud and loose on top, Revalia gives way to Farro, whose stroke ends are as wide as the middle and whose ascenders are compressed. Revalia is best at showing off, while Farro just keeps going.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-fragment-mono: Fragment Mono lines its letters up like nails on a ruler, with a tall waist line and no thick-and-thin contrast. Over a long page it hums as a flat gray, while Revalia stays out front.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-geist-mono: A tall band of letters with short stalks above gives Revalia its look, wide and bold in its stride. Geist Mono handles the quiet, fixed-width work, laying out code-style lowercase with big side gaps.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-genos: Expressive and loud, Revalia stretches its letters wide across the top of the page, with an open-tailed g. And Genos tucks in below, its glyphs pressed so close that edges almost kiss.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-geom: Approachable and a bit cheeky together, Revalia's wide-striding letters sit above Geom, whose lofty lowercase band stays easy to follow. Geom is a plain sans that reads smoothly line after line.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-hammersmith-one: Bold, with an open-tailed g and wide-spaced letters, Revalia sits above Hammersmith One, whose rounded strokes look like cut lengths of cord. And the bent-wire letters keep the page tidy under the shouting.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-inder: Short stalks above a tall band of letters mark Revalia, which strides widely across the line. And Inder, a plain sans with little height difference between cases, does the quieter work of simply reading.
